findings.issue: _parse_content_encoded returns a dict with key 'paragraphs' (not 'paragraphs_flat'). The task's What-to-do step 3 and TDD Anchor say to 'parse via _parse_content_encoded → получить blocks и paragraphs_flat'. The internal variable paragraphs_flat is never exposed in the return dict — it is assigned to body_paragraphs and returned as 'paragraphs'. Any test code that accesses result['paragraphs_flat'] will raise KeyError at runtime. Verified by reading orangetrack_source.py lines 575-612.
findings.fix: Replace 'paragraphs_flat' with 'paragraphs' everywhere in Task 4 descriptions and TDD Anchor that refer to the return value of _parse_content_encoded. The integration test should access result['paragraphs'] (or result['blocks']) from the returned dict.

findings.issue: _parse_content_encoded is not imported in the existing test file. The existing tests/test_orangetrack_source.py imports only: OrangetrackPingAggregator, _has_empty_embed_wrapper, _is_allowed_orangetrack_url, _safe_for_ping, _video_embed_url, fetch_orangetrack_article (lines 22-29). All existing tests call fetch_orangetrack_article, not _parse_content_encoded. The task instructs the agent to use _parse_content_encoded for all new unit tests, but omits the instruction to add it to the import list.
findings.fix: Add 'from orangetrack_source import _parse_content_encoded' (or use 'ots._parse_content_encoded') in the test file. The function exists at orangetrack_source.py:372 and is importable — this is a missing instruction, not a missing function.

findings.issue: The integration test description says to call preview_nodes with positional args: 'preview_nodes(title, paragraphs, images, source_url=..., subtitle, blocks)'. In the actual signature (telegraph_publisher.py:253), subtitle comes BEFORE blocks and source_url is positional. However, passing 'subtitle' as positional AFTER 'source_url=' as keyword creates a syntax conflict: keyword argument followed by positional. The example in the task mixes positional and keyword in an ambiguous way that may cause a SyntaxError if the agent copies it literally. Actual signature: preview_nodes(title, paragraphs=None, images=None, source_url=None, subtitle='', blocks=None, auto_marker=False).
findings.fix: In the task description, clarify that all non-title args must be passed as keyword arguments to avoid confusion. Example: preview_nodes(title='...', paragraphs=None, images=None, source_url='https://orangetrackdiecast.com/article', subtitle='', blocks=blocks).

findings.issue: Existing test test_runs_are_metadata_not_rendered_inline (test_telegraph_publisher.py:167) asserts that _build_content_from_blocks with source_url=None returns plain text even when runs contain hrefs. This test will still pass after Task 3 IF the implementation correctly handles source_url=None (skips link rendering). However, if Task 3's _render_paragraph_with_runs calls urlparse(source_url) when source_url=None, it will raise a TypeError or AttributeError. Task 5 adds tests for a 'new' helper but makes no mention of verifying the existing test remains green under the new implementation. The task must explicitly call out that source_url=None must be handled gracefully by the helper (returning plain text), and the existing test serves as a regression check for this exact scenario.
findings.fix: Add to Task 5 AC: 'Existing test test_runs_are_metadata_not_rendered_inline remains green — verifies source_url=None produces plain text.' Confirm in the task context that Task 3 must guard against source_url=None before calling urlparse.

findings.issue: The overlapping-runs implementation hint (Task 5, Details section) shows: block.text='ABCDE', run1=BCD, run2=CDE → expected children ['A', BCD, 'E']. The hint claims 'second appears plain' but the expected output has no 'CDE' as a plain text string — only 'E' appears after the node. The text of run2 ('CDE') is partly inside the ('CD') and partly in the trailing 'E'. This does not illustrate 'second appears plain as its own segment'; it shows the overlap absorbs run2's text into surrounding segments. The hint is misleading — an implementor following it literally may produce a different (also valid) interpretation of 'second appears plain', such as inserting 'CDE' as a separate plain string after the node.
findings.fix: Replace the overlapping-runs example with a clearer one where run2's text falls ENTIRELY after run1's span, so 'second appears plain' is unambiguous. Alternatively, annotate the example: 'Note: run2.text CDE is not inserted as a separate plain string — the overlap means positions 2-4 are already rendered inside BCD; only position 4 (E) is a new segment.'

findings.issue: Task 5 DoS-test hint says to assert 'any("DoS" in r.message or "skipped" in r.message ... for r in caplog.records)' — the exact WARNING message text is unknown at task-writing time and must be inferred from Task 3 implementation. The hint correctly defers to 'уточнить из реализации Task 3', but the placeholder assertion string ('DoS' or 'skipped') may not match what Task 3 actually logs, causing the test to be vacuously True or False. This is a test quality risk.
findings.fix: After Task 3 is implemented, confirm the actual WARNING message format and pin the assertion to a substring that will definitely appear (e.g., 'too large' or 'fallback'). Until then, the hint should instruct the agent to read the Task 3 WARNING log call and match that string.

The Verification Steps include a shell test: 'test -s work/orangetrack-rendering-fixes/logs/working/wave-3-code-audit.md' — this uses a relative path. Depending on where the agent's cwd is set, this could fail. The absolute path would be /workspaces/debian-2/my-hw/work/orangetrack-rendering-fixes/logs/working/wave-3-code-audit.md.
findings.fix: In Task 6 Verification Steps, replace 'test -s work/...' with 'test -s /workspaces/debian-2/my-hw/work/orangetrack-rendering-fixes/logs/working/wave-3-code-audit.md' or document the expected cwd.
